content.text: We cannot judge a premise until we know what it means. Language has four main uses: to assert, to ask, to command and to express feeling.
Logic works with assertions, because only an assertion is true or false.

examples.title: Four uses
examples.note: Only the assertion can be true or false.

examples.title: An unclear premise
lines: If there is a cosmic force, then the universe has a purpose.
examples.conclusion: So the universe has a purpose.
examples.note: The form is valid, but what is a cosmic force? We cannot accept or reject a premise we do not understand.

question.prompt: Which kind of sentence can be a premise?
question.hint: A premise has to be true or false. Which kind of sentence can be?
question.explanation: Only assertions are true or false, so premises and conclusions are assertions.
